assumptions: The actual checked fixed-integer target, signedness and width determine this monomorphic parser and Result layout.
Decimal FromStr accepts an optional ASCII plus sign, and signed targets also accept minus; no whitespace trimming or JavaScript numeric coercion is introduced.
Invalid digits are checked before reporting multiplication overflow at that byte; a preceding digit overflow stops before any later invalid byte.
Machine integers remain BigInt; usize/isize aliases use the existing checked 64-bit portable profile.
FromStr and str.parse are not const-eligible; stable from_str_radix is const-eligible since Rust 1.82, with invalid radix preserving source panic behavior.
NonZero types, binary32/binary64 FromStr, generic unbound parse targets and unchecked mutation require separate contracts.
No Rust execution or complete Router parity is established by these source-derived adapters.

trim uses Unicode White_Space; ASCII folds preserve non-ASCII scalars; len uses UTF-8 bytes and chars().count uses Unicode scalars

Pinned pure semantic profile: Rust 1.89.0 core/time.rs, stable functions only; clocks and Tokio sleep require separate checked effects. Duration values are immutable tagged records with own u64 BigInt seconds and normalized u32 BigInt nanoseconds below 1000000000; private fields describe the lowering ABI, not source-level constructor permission. Checked operations return frozen Rust Option values; ordinary operation overflow and invalid float constructors abort as Rust panics, never synthetic successful Results. Source f64 conversions preserve IEEE-754 values and nearest-nanosecond ties-to-even; f32 contracts are omitted until the frontend distinguishes binary32. constEligible means the pinned source declares the function const; pure alone never grants const evaluation to trait or floating constructor methods. Source-derived fixtures establish the adapter subset; Rust differential execution stays gated on complete JavaScript checks.
